title: Human and animal dominance hierarchies show a pyramidal structure guiding adult and infant social inferences

claims.claim: Triadic-pyramid prevalence test for human children
claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.evidence: https://osf.io/download/vmjf4/ — §2.1 Overall Computational Reproducibility, PDF pp. 3–4 and Table 1 Original columns: “all key results”.
claims.rationale: The report section 2.1 supports the match judgement through a general original-analysis reproduction statement. Its Original column quotes article values, and the shipped CSV only corroborates at two significant figures. No independent rerun at the full printed precision is established; reference_recomputed remains null.

diagnostic_results.evidence: Author package Pyramids_analysis_NHB_revision/Study 1a/tableS3.csv, pattern X021D, p.adj; report https://osf.io/download/vmjf4/ section 2.1 confirms reproduction generally.
diagnostic_results.scope: CSV rounded to two significant figures; corroboration only, not a recomputation at the full printed precision of Supplementary Table 2

claims.second_labeller_rationale: Report states all key results reproduce (section 2.1). Its Table 1 'Original' column (captioned as the paper's values, so possibly quoted rather than re-run) and the authors' shipped tableS3.csv output both agree with the printed value, at 3 sf and 2 sf respectively.

notes.sol: The source reproduces the original normalization and its reported outputs. Its Correctly Normalized column is a changed analysis and is excluded. Source comparison p-values are rounded more coarsely than original Supplementary Table 2; no invented high-precision reference values are supplied. Round 1: the report Table 1 Original column is a quotation of article values. The shipped tableS3.csv has only two significant figures, recorded as diagnostic_results; no extra precision is imputed to reference_recomputed.
notes.claude: Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: Values confirmed in the published Supplementary Information (static-content.springer.com, MOESM1, Supplementary Table 2). The report's Table 1 'Original' column is captioned as 'the original calculations in the paper', so it may quote the paper rather than show the re-run output; the reproduction verdict comes from the general statement in section 2.1. Its 'Original' tree p-value for human children (1.51e-1) differs from the printed 1.1520e-01, probably a transcription slip; trees are not claimed. The code sets set.seed(123) before the 1000-replicate Monte Carlo z-scores, so the values are deterministic. Mislabelling in the deposit and SI (P3, no numeric consequence): printed Supplementary Table 2 values are the one-sample Wilcoxon tests of normalized z-scores vs 0 (ST1a_plots.R writes these to 'tableS3.csv'), whereas the shipped 'tableS2.csv' holds the paired pyramid-vs-tree test, and the SI Table 2 caption describes the paired test. A checker matching by file name will find different numbers. The report's Z-score normalization finding (code normalizes across metrics within study, unlike the text's equation 3) is a code-vs-description inconsistency. It does not stop the shipped code reproducing the printed values, but a reconciler could treat it as a P2/P3 methods-description issue.
